# Business request: staff performance appraisals

## Background

We use webERP for sales, stock, manufacturing and the ledger, and we already
keep our staff in it: each person's manager, their labour item and normal
hours, their login, and their weekly timesheets. Appraisals are done today in
spreadsheets that HR chases by email. We want them in webERP, on the same
staff records, so HR, managers and staff work from one place.

## What we need

1. **Staff details for HR.** For every member of staff HR needs to record
   the department they work in (our departments are already set up in
   webERP), their job title, the date they started, and whether they are
   still with us. People who have left are kept, but are no longer due for
   appraisals.

2. **What staff are appraised on.** HR maintains a list of criteria (for
   example "Quality of work", "Teamwork"). Each criterion has a weight, and
   applies either to every job title or to one job title only. A criterion
   that has been used in an appraisal cannot be deleted, only retired.

3. **The rating scale.** Each criterion is rated 1 to 5: 1 Unsatisfactory,
   2 Needs improvement, 3 Meets expectations, 4 Exceeds expectations,
   5 Outstanding.

4. **Starting an appraisal.** HR starts an appraisal for a member of staff,
   either an annual one or a mid-year one, with the date it is due. The
   reviewer is the person's manager by default; HR may choose another
   reviewer, but the reviewer must be someone above the person in the
   reporting line (their manager, their manager's manager, and so on). The
   reviewer is told by email that the appraisal is waiting for them, with a
   link to it.

5. **Doing an appraisal.** The reviewer sees the appraisals waiting for
   them, rates the person on each criterion that applies to their job title,
   adds a comment per criterion and an overall comment, and can save and
   come back. When the reviewer completes it, the overall result is the
   weighted average of the ratings, rounded to the nearest point of the
   scale and shown with its label. Until an appraisal is completed its
   overall result shows as "Not rated". HR can cancel an appraisal that has
   not been completed. A completed appraisal cannot be changed. When it is
   completed, the person appraised is told by email.

6. **Appraisals due.** HR wants a list of staff due an appraisal: everyone
   still with us whose last completed annual appraisal is older than the
   appraisal frequency, or who has never had one, and who has no appraisal
   open now. The frequency, in months, is a company setting HR can change;
   it starts at 12. A mid-year appraisal is due six months after the last
   annual one.

7. **My appraisals.** Any member of staff who logs in to webERP can see
   their own completed appraisals, read only: the criteria, ratings,
   comments and overall result. They do not see appraisals that are still
   open or were cancelled, and never anyone else's.

8. **Keeping the records whole.** A member of staff who has appraisals, or
   a department that has staff in it, cannot be deleted. Changes to
   appraisals must be traceable in the same way as changes to other records
   in webERP.

9. **Who can do what.** Setting up criteria and the frequency, starting and
   cancelling appraisals and the due list are for HR. Doing an appraisal is
   for reviewers; seeing one's own appraisals is for every member of staff.
   Our administrator decides which roles get each of these, the same way as
   for the rest of webERP.

10. **The usual.** It must work on a new installation and on an upgrade of
    an existing one, read and write dates in each user's date format, be
    translatable like the rest of webERP, and be described in the manual.

//    https://github.com/timschofield/webERP/discussions/812
//      - Parts&Vendors allows 50 char
//      - @pakricard OpenCart store allows 64 char
// 
// 1. delete foreign key constraints (Bottom-Up-Drop aka BUD)
//
// SQL query to list foreign key constraints on stockmaster.stockid:
//
//     SELECT 
//         TABLE_NAME AS 'Referencing Table', 
//         COLUMN_NAME AS 'Foreign Key Column', 
//         CONSTRAINT_NAME AS 'Constraint Name'
//     FROM 
//         information_schema.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE
//     WHERE 
//         REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME = 'stockmaster' 
//         AND REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME = 'stockid'
//         AND TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE(); -- Limits results to your current webERP database
//
//   +-----------------------------+--------------------+------------------------------------+
//   | Referencing Table           | Foreign Key Column | Constraint Name                    |
//   +-----------------------------+--------------------+------------------------------------+
//   | bom                         | parent             | bom_ibfk_1                         |
//   | bom                         | component          | bom_ibfk_2                         |
//   | contractbom                 | stockid            | contractbom_ibfk_3                 |
//   | custitem                    | stockid            | custitem_ibfk_1                    |

//   | prices                      | stockid            | prices_ibfk_1                      |

Labour stock categories post the labour cost - the hours multipled by the item cost - to a balance sheet work in progress account and credit to a profit and loss account for the labour recovery.

(webERP handles the cost of sale of a stock item by posting (debiting) the cost to the cost of sales account and reducing (crediting) the stock value by the same amount.) $SQL = "SELECT `modulelink`,
				`reportlink` ,
				`modulename`
			FROM modules
			WHERE secroleid = '" . $_SESSION['AccessLevel'] . "'
			ORDER BY `sequence`";

	$ModuleLink[] = $MyRow['modulelink'];

$SQL = "SELECT `modulelink`,
				`menusection` ,
				`caption` ,
				`url`
			FROM menuitems
			WHERE secroleid = '" . $_SESSION['AccessLevel'] . "'
			ORDER BY `sequence`, `menusection`";
$Result = DB_query($SQL);

while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
	$MenuItems[$MyRow['modulelink']][$MyRow['menusection']]['Caption'][] = __($MyRow['caption']);
	$MenuItems[$MyRow['modulelink']][$MyRow['menusection']]['URL'][] = $MyRow['url'];
}

  `appraisalid` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `employeeid` int NOT NULL,
  `reviewerid` int NOT NULL,
  `appraisaltype` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1' COMMENT '1 annual, 2 mid-year',
  `status` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0' COMMENT '0 open, 1 completed, 2 cancelled',
  `startdate` date NOT NULL,
  `duedate` date NOT NULL,
  `startedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `completeddate` date DEFAULT NULL,
  `jobtitle` varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Job title of the person when the appraisal was completed',

  CONSTRAINT `appraisals_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`employeeid`) REFERENCES `employees` (`id`),
  CONSTRAINT `appraisals_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`reviewerid`) REFERENCES `employees` (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

<?php

// STAFF PERFORMANCE APPRAISALS

// 1. HR details on the existing staff records
AddColumn('departmentid', 'employees', 'INT', ' NULL', '', 'email');
AddColumn('jobtitle', 'employees', 'VARCHAR(50)', ' NOT NULL', '', 'departmentid');
AddColumn('startdate', 'employees', 'DATE', ' NULL', '', 'jobtitle');
AddColumn('active', 'employees', 'TINYINT', ' NOT NULL', '1', 'startdate');
AddIndex(array('departmentid'), 'employees', 'departmentid');
AddConstraint('employees', 'employees_ibfk_1', 'departmentid', 'departments', 'departmentid');

// 2. Appraisal tables
CreateTable('appraisalcriteria', "CREATE TABLE `appraisalcriteria` (
  `criterionid` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `description` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `weight` decimal(8,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.00',
  `jobtitle` varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Empty means the criterion applies to every job title',
  `retired` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  PRIMARY KEY (`criterionid`),
  KEY `jobtitle` (`jobtitle`)
)");

CreateTable('appraisals', "CREATE TABLE `appraisals` (
  `appraisalid` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `employeeid` int NOT NULL,
  `reviewerid` int NOT NULL,
  `appraisaltype` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1' COMMENT '1 annual, 2 mid-year',
  `status` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0' COMMENT '0 open, 1 completed, 2 cancelled',
  `startdate` date NOT NULL,
  `duedate` date NOT NULL,
  `startedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `completeddate` date DEFAULT NULL,
  `jobtitle` varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Job title of the person when the appraisal was completed',
  `overallscore` decimal(6,3) DEFAULT NULL,
  `overallrating` tinyint DEFAULT NULL COMMENT 'NULL until completed',
  `overallcomment` text,
  PRIMARY KEY (`appraisalid`),
  KEY `employeeid` (`employeeid`),
  KEY `reviewerid` (`reviewerid`),
  KEY `status` (`status`),
  CONSTRAINT `appraisals_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`employeeid`) REFERENCES `employees` (`id`),
  CONSTRAINT `appraisals_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`reviewerid`) REFERENCES `employees` (`id`)
)");

CreateTable('appraisalscores', "CREATE TABLE `appraisalscores` (
  `appraisalid` int NOT NULL,
  `criterionid` int NOT NULL,
  `rating` tinyint DEFAULT NULL,
  `comment` text,
  `criteriondescription` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'Copied from the criterion when the appraisal is completed',
  `weight` decimal(8,2) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT 'Copied from the criterion when the appraisal is completed',
  PRIMARY KEY (`appraisalid`,`criterionid`),
  KEY `criterionid` (`criterionid`),
  CONSTRAINT `appraisalscores_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`appraisalid`) REFERENCES `appraisals` (`appraisalid`),
  CONSTRAINT `appraisalscores_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`criterionid`) REFERENCES `appraisalcriteria` (`criterionid`)
)");

// 3. Company setting: months between annual appraisals
NewConfigValue('AppraisalFrequencyMonths', '12');

// 4. Pages and security tokens
NewSecurityToken(21, 'Appraisals - HR administration');
NewSecurityToken(22, 'Appraisals - reviewers');
NewSecurityToken(23, 'Appraisals - own appraisals');

NewScript('AppraisalCriteria.php', 21);
NewScript('Appraisals.php', 21);
NewScript('AppraisalsDue.php', 21);
NewScript('AppraisalReview.php', 22);
NewScript('MyAppraisals.php', 23);

// The administrator decides who gets the tokens. As a starting point the roles that can administer users
// get the HR and reviewer tokens, and every role other than the customer and supplier log on roles can see
// its own appraisals.
$RolesResult = DB_query("SELECT DISTINCT secroleid FROM securitygroups WHERE tokenid=15");
while ($RoleRow = DB_fetch_array($RolesResult)) {
	foreach (array(21, 22) as $TokenID) {
		InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array($RoleRow['secroleid'], $TokenID), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array($RoleRow['secroleid'], $TokenID));
	}
}
$RolesResult = DB_query("SELECT DISTINCT secroleid FROM securitygroups WHERE tokenid NOT IN (0, 1, 9)");
while ($RoleRow = DB_fetch_array($RolesResult)) {
	InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array($RoleRow['secroleid'], 23), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array($RoleRow['secroleid'], 23));
}

// 5. Menu links
NewMenuItem('manuf', 'Maintenance', __('Appraisal Criteria'), '/AppraisalCriteria.php', 10);
NewMenuItem('manuf', 'Transactions', __('Staff Appraisals'), '/Appraisals.php', 5);
NewMenuItem('manuf', 'Transactions', __('Conduct Appraisals'), '/AppraisalReview.php', 6);
NewMenuItem('manuf', 'Reports', __('Appraisals Due'), '/AppraisalsDue.php', 19);
NewMenuItem('manuf', 'Reports', __('My Appraisals'), '/MyAppraisals.php', 20);

if ($_SESSION['Updates']['Errors'] == 0) {
	UpdateDBNo(basename(__FILE__, '.php'), __('Staff performance appraisals'));
}

<?php

/* Functions shared by the staff appraisal scripts */

define('APPRAISAL_OPEN', 0);
define('APPRAISAL_COMPLETED', 1);
define('APPRAISAL_CANCELLED', 2);

define('APPRAISAL_ANNUAL', 1);
define('APPRAISAL_MIDYEAR', 2);

/**
 * The rating scale, keyed by the rating.
 */
function AppraisalRatingLabels() {
	return array(
		1 => __('Unsatisfactory'),
		2 => __('Needs improvement'),
		3 => __('Meets expectations'),
		4 => __('Exceeds expectations'),
		5 => __('Outstanding'),
	);
}

/**
 * The overall result as shown to the user: the rating and its label, or "Not rated" until the appraisal has been
 * completed.
 */
function AppraisalOverallText($Rating) {
	$Labels = AppraisalRatingLabels();
	if ($Rating === null or $Rating === '' or !isset($Labels[(int)$Rating])) {
		return __('Not rated');
	}
	return (int)$Rating . ' - ' . $Labels[(int)$Rating];
}

function AppraisalTypeLabels() {
	return array(
		APPRAISAL_ANNUAL => __('Annual'),
		APPRAISAL_MIDYEAR => __('Mid-year'),
	);
}

function AppraisalStatusLabels() {
	return array(
		APPRAISAL_OPEN => __('Open'),
		APPRAISAL_COMPLETED => __('Completed'),
		APPRAISAL_CANCELLED => __('Cancelled'),
	);
}

/**
 * The company setting: the number of months between annual appraisals.
 */
function GetAppraisalFrequency() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT confvalue FROM config WHERE confname='AppraisalFrequencyMonths'");
	$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	if ($Row and (int)$Row[0] > 0) {
		return (int)$Row[0];
	}
	return 12;
}

/**
 * The ids of the people above an employee in the reporting line, nearest first: the manager, the manager's
 * manager and so on. Stops if the reporting line loops back on itself.
 */
function GetReportingChain($EmployeeID) {
	$Chain = array();
	$Seen = array((int)$EmployeeID);
	$Current = (int)$EmployeeID;
	while (true) {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT manager FROM employees WHERE id='" . $Current . "'");
		$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		if (!$Row or (int)$Row[0] == 0 or in_array((int)$Row[0], $Seen)) {
			break;
		}
		$Current = (int)$Row[0];
		$Seen[] = $Current;
		$Chain[] = $Current;
	}
	return $Chain;
}

/**
 * Reads a date typed by the user in their date format. Returns the date in SQL format or false if it is not a
 * valid date.
 */
function AppraisalDateToSQL($Input) {
	$Input = trim($Input);
	if ($Input == '') {
		return false;
	}
	if (mb_strlen($Input) == 10 and EnsureSQLDateFormat($Input)) {
		return $Input;
	}
	if (!Is_Date($Input)) {
		return false;
	}
	$Parts = explode('-', FormatDateForSQL($Input));
	if (count($Parts) != 3 or !checkdate((int)$Parts[1], (int)$Parts[2], (int)$Parts[0])) {
		return false;
	}
	return sprintf('%04d-%02d-%02d', (int)$Parts[0], (int)$Parts[1], (int)$Parts[2]);
}

/**
 * Adds whole months to an SQL date, stopping at the end of the month rather than spilling into the next one
 * (31 January plus one month is the last day of February).
 */
function AppraisalAddMonths($SQLDate, $Months) {
	$Date = new DateTime($SQLDate);
	$Day = (int)$Date->format('j');
	$Date->setDate((int)$Date->format('Y'), (int)$Date->format('n'), 1);
	$Date->modify('+' . (int)$Months . ' months');
	$Date->setDate((int)$Date->format('Y'), (int)$Date->format('n'), min($Day, (int)$Date->format('t')));
	return $Date->format('Y-m-d');
}

/**
 * The weighted average of the ratings and that average rounded to the nearest point of the scale.
 *
 * @param array $Rows rows having the keys weight and rating
 * @return array|false array(score, rating), or false if there is nothing to average
 */
function AppraisalOverallResult($Rows) {
	$TotalWeight = 0;
	$WeightedTotal = 0;
	foreach ($Rows as $Row) {
		$TotalWeight += $Row['weight'];
		$WeightedTotal += $Row['weight'] * $Row['rating'];
	}
	if ($TotalWeight <= 0) {
		return false;
	}
	// round first to get rid of binary fractions that would push an exact half to the wrong side
	$Score = round($WeightedTotal / $TotalWeight, 6);
	return array($Score, (int)round($Score, 0, PHP_ROUND_HALF_UP));
}

/**
 * The criteria an employee is appraised on: those not retired that apply to every job title or to the job title
 * of the employee.
 */
function AppraisalCriteriaFor($JobTitle) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT criterionid,

	);
}

/**

 */
function GetAppraisalFrequency() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT confvalue FROM config WHERE confname='AppraisalFrequencyMonths'");
	$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);

		return (int)$Row[0];

		if (!$Row or (int)$Row[0] == 0 or in_array((int)$Row[0], $Seen)) {
			break;
		}
		$Current = (int)$Row[0];
		$Seen[] = $Current;
		$Chain[] = $Current;
	}
	return $Chain;
}

function AppraisalOverallResult($Rows) {

"'"); if (DB_num_rows($EmployeeResult) == 0) { $InputError = 1; prnMsg(__('The member of staff to be appraised must be selected'), 'error'); } else { $EmployeeRow = DB_fetch_array($EmployeeResult); if ($EmployeeRow['active'] != 1) { $InputError = 1; prnMsg(__('This person has left, so they are not due appraisals'), 'error'); } } if ($_POST['AppraisalType'] != APPRAISAL_ANNUAL and $_POST['AppraisalType'] != APPRAISAL_MIDYEAR) { $InputError = 1; prnMsg(__('The type of appraisal must be annual or mid-year'), 'error'); } $DueDateSQL = AppraisalDateToSQL($_POST['DueDate']); if ($DueDateSQL === false) { $InputError = 1; prnMsg(__('The date the appraisal is due must be entered as a valid date in the format') . ' ' . $_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat'], 'error'); } if ($InputError == 0) { // the reviewer is the manager unless HR chose someone else further up the reporting line $Chain = GetReportingChain($SelectedEmployee); if (isset($_POST['ReviewerID']) and $_POST['ReviewerID'] != '') { $ReviewerID = (int)$_POST['ReviewerID']; } elseif (count($Chain) > 0) { $ReviewerID = $Chain[0]; } else { $ReviewerID = 0; } if (!in_array($ReviewerID, $Chain)) { $InputError = 1; prnMsg(__('The reviewer must be above the person in the reporting line: their manager, their manager\'s manager, and so on'), 'error'); } else { $ReviewerResult = DB_query("SELECT id, firstname, surname, email, userid, active FROM employees WHERE id='" . $ReviewerID . <?php

/* Functions shared by the staff appraisal scripts */

define('APPRAISAL_OPEN', 0);
define('APPRAISAL_COMPLETED', 1);
define('APPRAISAL_CANCELLED', 2);

define('APPRAISAL_ANNUAL', 1);
define('APPRAISAL_MIDYEAR', 2);

/**
 * The rating scale, keyed by the rating.
 */
function AppraisalRatingLabels() {
	return array(
		1 => __('Unsatisfactory'),
		2 => __('Needs improvement'),
		3 => __('Meets expectations'),
		4 => __('Exceeds expectations'),
		5 => __('Outstanding'),
	);
}

/**
 * The overall result as shown to the user: the rating and its label, or "Not rated" until the appraisal has been
 * completed.
 */
function AppraisalOverallText($Rating) {
	$Labels = AppraisalRatingLabels();
	if ($Rating === null or $Rating === '' or !isset($Labels[(int)$Rating])) {
		return __('Not rated');
	}
	return (int)$Rating . ' - ' . $Labels[(int)$Rating];
}

function AppraisalTypeLabels() {
	return array(
		APPRAISAL_ANNUAL => __('Annual'),
		APPRAISAL_MIDYEAR => __('Mid-year'),
	);
}

function AppraisalStatusLabels() {
	return array(
		APPRAISAL_OPEN => __('Open'),
		APPRAISAL_COMPLETED => __('Completed'),
		APPRAISAL_CANCELLED => __('Cancelled'),
	);
}

/**
 * The company setting: the number of months between annual appraisals.
 */
function GetAppraisalFrequency() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT confvalue FROM config WHERE confname='AppraisalFrequencyMonths'");
	$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	if ($Row and (int)$Row[0] > 0) {
		return (int)$Row[0];
	}
	return 12;
}

/**
 * The ids of the people above an employee in the reporting line, nearest first: the manager, the manager's
 * manager and so on. Stops if the reporting line loops back on itself.
 */
function GetReportingChain($EmployeeID) {
	$Chain = array();
	$Seen = array((int)$EmployeeID);
	$Current = (int)$EmployeeID;
	while (true) {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT manager FROM employees WHERE id='" . $Current . "'");
		$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
		if (!$Row or (int)$Row[0] == 0 or in_array((int)$Row[0], $Seen)) {
			break;
		}
		$Current = (int)$Row[0];
		$Seen[] = $Current;
		$Chain[] = $Current;
	}
	return $Chain;
}

/**
 * Reads a date typed by the user in their date format. Returns the date in SQL format or false if it is not a
 * valid date.
 */
function AppraisalDateToSQL($Input) {
	$Input = trim($Input);
	if ($Input == '') {
		return false;
	}
	if (mb_strlen($Input) == 10 and EnsureSQLDateFormat($Input)) {
		return $Input;
	}
	if (!Is_Date($Input)) {
		return false;
	}
	$Parts = explode('-', FormatDateForSQL($Input));
	if (count($Parts) != 3 or !checkdate((int)$Parts[1], (int)$Parts[2], (int)$Parts[0])) {
		return false;
	}
	return sprintf('%04d-%02d-%02d', (int)$Parts[0], (int)$Parts[1], (int)$Parts[2]);
}

/**
 * Adds whole months to an SQL date, stopping at the end of the month rather than spilling into the next one
 * (31 January plus one month is the last day of February).
 */
function AppraisalAddMonths($SQLDate, $Months) {
	$Date = new DateTime($SQLDate);
	$Day = (int)$Date->format('j');
	$Date->setDate((int)$Date->format('Y'), (int)$Date->format('n'), 1);
	$Date->modify('+' . (int)$Months . ' months');
	$Date->setDate((int)$Date->format('Y'), (int)$Date->format('n'), min($Day, (int)$Date->format('t')));
	return $Date->format('Y-m-d');
}

/**
 * The weighted average of the ratings and that average rounded to the nearest point of the scale.
 *
 * @param array $Rows rows having the keys weight and rating
 * @return array|false array(score, rating), or false if there is nothing to average
 */
function AppraisalOverallResult($Rows) {
	$TotalWeight = 0;
	$WeightedTotal = 0;
	foreach ($Rows as $Row) {
		$TotalWeight += $Row['weight'];
		$WeightedTotal += $Row['weight'] * $Row['rating'];
	}
	if ($TotalWeight <= 0) {
		return false;
	}
	// round first to get rid of binary fractions that would push an exact half to the wrong side
	$Score = round($WeightedTotal / $TotalWeight, 6);
	return array($Score, (int)round($Score, 0, PHP_ROUND_HALF_UP));
}

/**
 * The criteria an employee is appraised on: those not retired that apply to every job title or to the job title
 * of the employee.
 */
function AppraisalCriteriaFor($JobTitle) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT criterionid,
								description,
								weight
						FROM appraisalcriteria
						WHERE retired=0
						AND (jobtitle='' OR jobtitle='" . DB_escape_string($JobTitle) . "')
						ORDER BY description, criterionid");
	$Criteria = array();
	while ($Row = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Criteria[$Row['criterionid']] = $Row;
	}
	return $Criteria;
}

/**
 * The address of a script, as it should be written in an email.
 */
function AppraisalLink($Script, $Parameters = '') {
	global $RootPath;
	$Scheme = (!empty($_SERVER['HTTPS']) and $_SERVER['HTTPS'] != 'off') ? 'https' : 'http';
	$URL = $Scheme . '://' . $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] . $RootPath . '/' . $Script;
	if ($Parameters != '') {
		$URL .= '?' . $Parameters;
	}
	return $URL;
}

/**
 * The employee records belonging to the logged in webERP user.
 */
function AppraisalEmployeeIDsOfUser() {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT id FROM employees WHERE userid='" . $_SESSION['UserID'] . "'");
	$IDs = array();
	while ($Row = DB_fetch_row($Result)) {
		$IDs[] = (int)$Row[0];
	}
	return $IDs;
}

Each employee also has the details HR needs for appraisals: the department they work in (departments are set up under Departments in the set up menu), their job title, the date they started and whether they are still employed. Dates are entered and shown in the date format of the user. When an employee leaves, clear Still Employed - the record is kept, but the person is no longer due appraisals. An employee who has appraisals cannot be deleted, and neither can a department that has employees in it. The manager of an employee cannot be someone who reports to that employee.

Staff Appraisals

Staff appraisals are done on the same employee records that are used for timesheets, so HR, managers and staff work from one place. An appraisal rates a member of staff on a list of criteria. Each criterion is rated on this scale:

1Unsatisfactory
2Needs improvement
3Meets expectations
4Exceeds expectations
5Outstanding

Who can do what is decided by the webERP administrator through the security roles. Three security tokens are used: Appraisals - HR administration (criteria, the frequency, starting and cancelling appraisals and the list of appraisals due), Appraisals - reviewers (doing the appraisals that are waiting) and Appraisals - own appraisals (seeing one's own completed appraisals). Changes to appraisals are recorded in the audit trail like changes to other records.

Criteria and the appraisal frequency

HR maintains the criteria under Appraisal Criteria in the Manufacturing maintenance menu, for example "Quality of work" or "Teamwork". Each criterion has a weight - how much it counts towards the overall result - and applies either to every job title (leave the job title empty) or to one job title only. A criterion that has been used in an appraisal cannot be deleted, only retired; a retired criterion is not used in appraisals from then on, and can be put back into use again.

The same screen holds the company setting months between annual appraisals. It starts at 12.

Starting an appraisal

HR starts an appraisal under Staff Appraisals: select the member of staff, choose an annual or a mid-year appraisal and enter the date it is due. The reviewer is the person's manager unless HR chooses someone else - the reviewer must be above the person in the reporting line (their manager, their manager's manager and so on). The reviewer must still be employed and must be a webERP user. A person can only have one appraisal that is open at a time. The reviewer is told by email that the appraisal is waiting, with a link to it. HR can cancel an appraisal that has not been completed from the same screen.

Doing an appraisal

Reviewers see the appraisals waiting for them under Conduct Appraisals. The reviewer rates the person on each criterion that applies to their job title (the criteria that apply to every job title and those for their job title), adds a comment for each criterion and an overall comment. Save keeps what has been entered so that the reviewer can come back later. When the reviewer chooses Complete Appraisal every criterion must have been rated. The overall result is the weighted average of the ratings, rounded to the nearest point of the scale (a half rounds up), and is shown with its label, for example "4 - Exceeds expectations". Until an appraisal is completed the overall result is shown as "Not rated". A completed appraisal cannot be changed, and the person who was appraised is told by email.

Appraisals due

Appraisals Due lists the staff who are due an appraisal: everyone still employed who has no appraisal open and whose last completed annual appraisal is older than the appraisal frequency, or who has never had one. A mid-year appraisal is due six months after the last annual appraisal. Each line has a link to start the appraisal.

My appraisals

Every member of staff who logs in to webERP - and whose employee record is linked to their webERP user - can see their own completed appraisals under My Appraisals: the criteria, ratings, comments and the overall result. They cannot change them. Appraisals that are still open or were cancelled, and appraisals of other people, are never shown.

Labour Recording

Overview

The cost of labour is of course a major component of the cost of manufactured items. A method is required to capture the cost of the labour spent in the process of manufacture.

The work done on work orders and contracts can be captured by the entry of time-sheets. Each employee defined can have a time-sheet - this has nothing to do with payroll - it is about capturing the time/cost of employees against work orders.

The cost associated with employees is set by associating the employee with an item. The labour item has the cost set at an amount that should recover both the manufacturing wage/salary costs (and typically manufacturing overheads). A special type of item can be defined for labour - these items must have a labour type stock category. It is the (labour) stock category record that defines how the labour cost is posted in the general ledger.

Labour stock categories post the labour cost - the hours multipled by the item cost - to a balance sheet work in progress account and credit to a profit and loss account for the labour recovery.

Typically, the actual labour cost from the payroll is debited to the profit and loss account wages/salaries costs - the labour recovery takes this cost from the profit and loss (as a credit) and puts it into stock - until the manufactured items are sold. (webERP handles the cost of sale of a stock item by posting (debiting) the cost to the cost of sales account and reducing (crediting) the stock value by the same amount.) The profit and loss account showing the manufacturing costs would look something like the below example:

AccountAmount
Wages10,000
Repairs and Maintenance2,000
Power1,000
Rent5,000
____________
TOTAL MANUFACTURING COSTS18,000
Labour recoveries - 400 hours @ $50(20,000)
____________
NET under/(over) recovery(2,000)
____________

The over recovery represents the adjustment to the gross profit required due to the fact that more manufacturing cost was recovered into the cost of stock manufactured in the month than was incurred. Typically, if manufacturing work is greater than budgeted then the overheads are spread more thinly over a greater amount of work - naturally, this results in an over recovery of manufacturing costs. However, if labour is not so productive and the volume of work is less than budgeted then this will result in an under-recovery of manufacturing costs.

Setting Up Employees

Labour in webERP is actually a special type of item - this allows the routings to be defined in the bill of materials along with all the other physical components. Labour items are simply stock items that have a stock category that is a labour type. Child items of labour type stock categories are all labour items. The first step to setup labour is to setup a labour type stock catergory. Since the GL posting for labour is set up at this level a labour type stock category is required for each type of labour that needs to be posted to a different GL account. e.g. perhaps and engineering firm has a separate cost centre for engineering labour/cost from it"s manufacturing - in this case engineering labour would require a separate labour type.

Note that the stock category screen changes when the stock type is set to "Labour" now, what was the stock account for a normal stock category becomes the labour "recovery" account - this is now a profit and loss GL account where the labour costs are credited to. Note that the stock adjustments account will never be used for dummy/service or labour type stock categories as these will never have physical quantites of stock held. Hence no adjustment will ever be required! Also, what was the

Once the labour type stock category is defined any number of labour type items can be defined like any other stock item. However, since each employee is mapped to a particular labour item it is only necessary to define labour type items for each category of labour where they will have a different cost. Perhaps tradesfolk, apprentices, supervisors may be set up with different costs - but all posted in the GL on the same basis using the same labour stock category.

Having set up the necessary labour stock categories and labour items in those categories, then the employees can be defined

# Staff performance appraisals - notes

Nothing could be run here (no shell, no database, no browser), so none of this has been executed. It was written
against the existing code and conventions and read back by eye only. It needs a test pass on a new install, on an
upgrade and in the browser before release.

## What changed and where

**Database**
- `sql/updates/44.php` - the upgrade: new columns on `employees`, three new tables, the config value, pages,
  security tokens, starting role assignments and menu links. Each step is re-runnable like the other updates.
- `install/sql/tables/employees.sql` (new columns plus a foreign key to `departments`), and new
  `appraisalcriteria.sql`, `appraisals.sql`, `appraisalscores.sql` - used by a new installation.
- `install/sql/data/{config,scripts,securitytokens,securitygroups,menuitems}.sql` and `install/sql/demo.sql` -
  the same rows added for a new installation (normal and demo), so new and upgraded databases match.
- `employees` gains `departmentid`, `jobtitle`, `startdate`, `active`.
  `appraisalcriteria` holds description, weight, job title (empty = every job title) and `retired`.
  `appraisals` holds person, reviewer, type (1 annual, 2 mid-year), status (0 open, 1 completed, 2 cancelled),
  dates, overall score/rating/comment. `appraisalscores` holds the rating and comment per criterion.
- Company setting: config key `AppraisalFrequencyMonths`, default 12.

**Scripts**
- `Employees.php` - department, job title, start date and "still employed" on the staff record; list shows them;
  delete is refused if the person has appraisals (as subject or reviewer); a person cannot be given a manager who
  reports to them. `Departments.php` - delete is refused while employees are in the department.
- `AppraisalCriteria.php` - criteria (add, edit, retire, use again, delete if never used) and the frequency. HR.
- `Appraisals.php` - start an appraisal (reviewer email), list all appraisals, cancel an open one. HR.
- `AppraisalsDue.php` - the due list with a link to start each appraisal. HR.
- `AppraisalReview.php` - reviewer's list of waiting appraisals; rate, comment, save, complete (email to the person).
- `MyAppraisals.php` - a member of staff's own completed appraisals, read only.
- `includes/AppraisalFunctions.php` - shared code (scale labels, reporting chain, date reading, weighted result,
  read-only display).
- `doc/Manual/ManualLabour.html`, `ManualOutline.php` - manual.

**Security**: new tokens 21 *Appraisals - HR administration* (criteria, frequency, start, cancel, due list),
22 *Appraisals - reviewers*, 23 *Appraisals - own appraisals*. Starting assignment only: 21 and 22 to the roles that
hold token 15 (system administrator), 23 to every role except the customer / supplier log-on roles. The administrator
changes this in the usual role screens. As for every other script, the menu links are added for all roles whether or
not the role holds the token.

**Audit trail**: all writes go through `DB_query`, which already records INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in `audittrail`, so
appraisal changes are traced like other records. No separate mechanism was added.

## Ambiguities and how I resolved them

- **Who the reviewer/person are in the system.** A person is an `employees` row; "logs in" is matched through
  `employees.userid`. A reviewer must have a webERP user (otherwise they could never do it) and must still be employed.
  If the default manager can't qualify, HR must pick someone else above them in the line; with nobody qualifying the
  appraisal can't be started.
- **Existing staff have no department / job title / start date.** The columns are nullable so the upgrade works;
  the Employees form requires all three whenever a record is saved.
- **"Never had one" is due immediately**, including a person who started yesterday. The request has no
  grace period for new starters, so I did not invent one.
- **"Older than the frequency"** means last completed annual appraisal date + N months is before today (end-of-month
  safe). Mid-year is due on or after last annual + 6 months, only if the annual one is not already due and no
  mid-year has been completed since that annual appraisal. Due list rows show which type is due.
- **Completion date** (not due date or start date) is what ageing uses.
- **Rounding**: the weighted average rounds half up (3.5 -> 4). Weights must be greater than zero.
- **Criteria for an appraisal** are worked out when the reviewer opens it/completes it: not retired, and for every job
  title or the person's current job title (case-insensitive). Completing needs all of them rated and at least one
  criterion. Description, weight and the job title are copied onto the completed appraisal, so later edits to a
  criterion do not change history. Draft ratings for criteria retired meanwhile are dropped on completion.
- **"Used in an appraisal"** = has a saved score row, including drafts and cancelled appraisals.
- **One open appraisal per person** is enforced when starting (the due list assumes it).
- **Cancelled/left people**: marking someone as having left does not cancel their open appraisals; HR can cancel them.
- **Reviewers' view** is limited to appraisals waiting for them (plus a just-completed one by link). HR sees status and
  overall result in the list but not the ratings; only the person appraised sees completed details on My Appraisals.
- **Dates** are typed and shown in the user's `DefaultDateFormat` (text inputs, validated with `Is_Date`), stored as SQL dates.
- **Menu**: placed in the Manufacturing module next to Employees/Timesheets, since there is no HR module.

## Not done / follow-ups

- The translation template (`.pot`) was not regenerated (no tooling here); all new text uses `__()`.
- `install/sql/tables/employees.sql` keeps `stockid varchar(20)` as it was; update 43 widens it on upgrades only
  (existing discrepancy, left alone).
- The root `sql/` legacy dumps and `sql/mysql/` upgrade scripts were not touched.
- The demo employees have no department/job title/start date; the form will ask for them on first edit.

The appraisals feature is written, but none of it has been run, because this session has no shell, database or browser. Nothing has been tested on a new install, an upgrade or in the browser. I only read it back against the existing code.

What now exists:
- **Staff details:** department, job title, start date and "still employed" on the employee record in `Employees.php`. A person with appraisals can't be deleted, and `Departments.php` refuses to delete a department that has staff in it. People marked as having left are kept and drop out of the due list.
- **Criteria and frequency:** `AppraisalCriteria.php` for HR. Criteria have a weight and apply to every job title or one. A criterion that has been used can only be retired. The frequency is a company setting, default 12 months.
- **Starting and cancelling:** `Appraisals.php` for HR. The reviewer defaults to the manager and can be changed only to someone above the person in the reporting line. The reviewer is emailed a link.
